newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran calls for broad-based government in Kabul.
newsitem.headline: Iran calls for broad-based government in Kabul.

text.p: Iranian Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati said prospects for peace in Afghanistan were poor without a broad-based government in Kabul, captured by the radical Islamic Taleban movement.

"Any government, any new government in Afghanistan should be a broad-based government. No ethnic group can run that country without an active contribution from the other ethnic groups. And no religious group can run the country without a contribution from the others," Velayati said.
"We are not very optimistic about the future of Afghanistan if this trend continues," he added.
His comments were broadcast on Sunday night on Iranian television, monitored by the British Broadcasting Corporation.

"So we have to think about a comprehensive peaceful settlement for Afghanistan. We do hope that the people of Afghanistan can decide about their own destiny without any foreign intervention," Velayati said.
He said Iran will continue to work for peace in Afghanistan. "We will continue our consultations with our friends, neighbouring countries to Afghanistan."
The fundamentalist Taleban, which captured the Afghan capital Kabul last month, have taken control of about two-thirds of the war-torn country, imposing a strict Islamic code.
A senior Iranian cleric on Friday accused Taleban of giving Islam a bad name by imposing "fossilised" policies and committing acts of violence.

Shi'ite Iran has supported the ousted government of President Burhanuddin Rabbani and was hostile to the Sunni fundamentalist Taleban. Iran's media has accused the Taleban of being manipulated by Pakistan and the United States.
Pakistan denies charges from Afghanistan's ousted government that Islamabad gave military help to the Taleban.
